title: Affine countability after tensoring with a perfect complex
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme], considered on its small etale site with structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and suppose that $\mathcal H^j(L)(Y)$ is countable for every $j\in\mathbf Z$. Let $Q\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ be perfect, meaning etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Then $H^nR\Gamma(Y,L\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Y}Q)$ is countable for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. Derived tensor uses K-flat resolutions and derived global sections use K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. No boundedness of $L$, Noetherian hypothesis on $A$, or countability of $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CRP (lemma-countable-cohomology), affine paragraph of the proof; small-etale interpretation explicitly used in spaces-perfect.tex Tag 0CRU (lemma-countable-cohomology), affine base case.

proof.text: First $Q$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. On an etale scheme cover choose the bounded local models in the hypothesis. The structure module is quasi-coherent by its one-generator presentation. A direct summand $F$ of $\mathcal O^r$, with inclusion $i$ and retraction $p$, is the kernel of $1-ip$ on $\mathcal O^r$. The kernel, image and cokernel assertions of [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits] therefore make each term, each cycle module, each boundary module and their cohomology quotient quasi-coherent. Exactness of etale restriction and the jointly surjective etale-cover test in [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus] imply that $Q$ itself has quasi-coherent cohomology. This supplies the essential-image hypothesis before applying the derived equivalence; perfectness alone is not silently taken as an input to that equivalence.

source.place: Tag 08JL (lemma-pseudo-coherent), perfect local-model case; Tag 08F2 (lemma-check-quasi-coherence-on-covering); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization], choose an unbounded $A$-module complex $M^\bullet$ and $a_A(M^\bullet)\simeq L$. Its cohomology and section comparisons give $H^j(M^\bullet)\cong\mathcal H^j(L)(Y)$, hence these modules have countable underlying sets. By [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison] and step 1, choose $Q_0\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y,\mathrm{Zar}})$ with $\epsilon_Y^*Q_0\simeq Q$. The reverse implication of [lem-sfb-etale-detects-perfect] makes $Q_0$ Zariski perfect. Apply [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] to obtain $Q_0\simeq\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ with $P^\bullet$ bounded and each $P^a$ finite projective over $A$. The associated-etale functor in the first citation is Zariski tilde followed by $\epsilon_Y^*$, so also $L\simeq\epsilon_Y^*\widetilde{M^\bullet}$. All comparisons here concern unbounded derived categories; the boundedness is only on $P^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0CRP (lemma-countable-cohomology), affine paragraph; Tags 06Z0 (lemma-affine-compare-bounded) and 08EB (lemma-perfect-affine); spaces-perfect.tex Tags 071Q and 08HG (lemma-descend-perfect).

proof.text:
Projective modules are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], so [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P^\bullet$ K-flat. The ordinary-module tensor computation [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] represents $P^\bullet\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M^\bullet$ by $T^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(P^\bullet\otimes_A M^\bullet)$; its terms and differential are the signed total tensor of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], on the one-object site for $A$-modules. Clause (3) of [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] gives $Q_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}\widetilde{M^\bullet}\simeq\widetilde{T^\bullet}$. Apply the derived pullback tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $\epsilon_Y$. Its pullback is exact by [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison], so its left derived functor is its termwise functor. Thus $Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\simeq a_A(T^\bullet)$. The inverse-comparison of [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] now yields an isomorphism in $D(A)$,
$$R\Gamma(Y,Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)\simeq T^\bullet.$$
This is an identification of derived objects, not just individual cohomology groups. No resolution of $M^\bullet$ with a boundedness condition has been used.

source.place: Tag 08DX (lemma-quasi-coherence-tensor-product), clause (2), and Tag 0CRP affine paragraph; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); more-algebra.tex Tag 064K.

proof.text:
Fix a degree $a$. Choose finitely many generators of $P^a$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], giving a surjection $p:A^r\to P^a$. The lifting characterization of [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], applied to $1_{P^a}$ and $p$, gives $i:P^a\to A^r$ with $pi=1$. Tensor these two maps with every term of $M^\bullet$. They are chain maps $P^a\otimes_A M^\bullet\to(M^\bullet)^r\to P^a\otimes_A M^\bullet$ with composite the identity, since the differentials here act only on $M^\bullet$. They induce an injection
$$H^j(P^a\otimes_A M^\bullet)\hookrightarrow H^j((M^\bullet)^r)=H^j(M^\bullet)^r.$$
The equality follows by taking kernels, images and quotients coordinate by coordinate in a finite direct sum. A finite product of countable sets is countable: take injections into $\mathbf N$ and then the usual injection $\mathbf N^r\to\mathbf N$ (including the singleton for $r=0$). Consequently every group on the left is countable. This argument uses neither countability of $A$ nor countability of the terms of $M^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0CRP (lemma-countable-cohomology), last two sentences of the affine paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 0518 (definition-finite) and 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective).

proof.text:
Choose $a\le b$ with $P^c=0$ outside $[a,b]$. For $c\le b+1$, set $T_c=\operatorname{Tot}((\sigma_{\ge c}P)\otimes_A M)$, where $\sigma_{\ge c}$ is the stupid truncation of [lem-sf-module-stupid-truncation-short-exact]. Tensor its short exact sequence with $M$ and totalize to obtain
$$0\longrightarrow T_{c+1}\longrightarrow T_c\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}(P^c[-c]\otimes_A M)\longrightarrow0.$$
This remains degreewise split exact: in each total degree inclusion inserts zero in the $P^c\otimes M$ coordinate and projection takes that coordinate. Both are chain maps because the upper tail is a subcomplex; the quotient differential is $(-1)^c(1\otimes d_M)$. Its degree-$n$ cohomology is $H^{n-c}(P^c\otimes M)$, countable by step 4 (the constant sign changes neither kernels nor images). Start with $T_{b+1}=0$ and descend through the finitely many integers $b,\ldots,a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact], $H^n(T_c)$ has kernel, under its map to the quotient cohomology, equal to the image of the countable $H^n(T_{c+1})$. This kernel is countable and the image in the quotient cohomology is countable. Choose one lift for each element of that image. The addition map from the product of the kernel and this set of lifts onto $H^n(T_c)$ is surjective, so $H^n(T_c)$ is countable. This proves the inductive claim for every $n$ simultaneously. In particular every $H^n(T_a)=H^n(T^\bullet)$ is countable.

source.place: Tag 0CRP (lemma-countable-cohomology), induction on the length of the finite projective complex; homology.tex Tag 0117 (lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain).

proof.text: Taking cohomology of the derived isomorphism in step 3 and using step 5 proves countability of $H^nR\Gamma(Y,Q\otimes^{\mathbf L}L)$. The canonical symmetry of derived tensor identifies this with the group in the statement, $H^nR\Gamma(Y,L\otimes^{\mathbf L}Q)$. The zero complex, empty spectrum ($A=0$), ranks zero and negative degrees are included: the zero case starts the same induction, and its interval length is finite independently of $n$.

Steps checked: (1) quasi-coherent cohomology of the étale-perfect Q via summand = ker(1-ip), 03M1 kernel/cokernel closure and the 08F2 cover test. (2) The 071Q realization a_A gives H^j(M)=H^j(L)(Y), countable; the ε^* equivalence gives Q_0, 08HG makes it Zariski perfect, 08EB gives Q_0 ≃ P̃. (3) P is K-flat (projective ⇒ flat, bounded flat ⇒ K-flat); the tensor model gives P⊗^L M = Tot; 08DX(3), the 07A4 pullback with exact ε^*, and the RΓ quasi-inverse give RΓ(Q⊗L) ≅ T in D(A). (4) The split surjection A^r→P^a gives an injection into H^j(M)^r. (5) The stupid-truncation SES is degreewise split; the long exact sequence and a countable-extension argument run over the finite interval, base T_{b+1}=0. (6) Tensor symmetry. Edge cases A=0, Q=0, a single term in a negative degree, unbounded M, uncountable A all work. No cycle. Batch 5: the four sfb qcoh/realization nodes reach only def-trf-algebraic-space (the general algebraic-space definition, already a stmt_dep), and etale-detects-perfect reaches only lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square (generic Zariski/étale module comparison, 03FH/03LC). Neither is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so it is acceptable. The generic pc/pbc/sf tool_uses are accepted. Advisory: Zariski D_QCoh is written with site quasi-coherence versus pqf-def-coherent, which is the same notion.
